opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write unless their role owns the system; Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is not permitted. Granting write as the maximum allowed.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E039 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training are limited to read on any system (never admin). Admin request exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: Belinda Fuentes (E039) requests admin to Payroll. Admin is not permitted under either set of facts: as a full-time Analyst, max is write (Analyst does not own Payroll, which is owned by the Payroll Specialist role); as a contractor with basic security training, max is read (never admin). The two notes conflict on employment type (HR: full-time; Security: contractor with basic training). Given the conflicting evidence, I grant the most restrictive allowable maximum, read, which is safe under both interpretations and never exceeds the policy or the requested level.

Security note says: employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Contractors with basic training limited to read. Grant read.

There's a conflict between the two notes: HR says full_time, Security says contractor.

My role: Approver. I need to make the final decision based on information available.

The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

For Payroll: owned by Payroll Specialist role. Employee is Analyst, so even if full-time, admin not allowed (max write). If contractor with basic training, max read.

So admin is above the maximum in both interpretations. The question is whether the maximum is write or read. Given conflicting facts, we need to determine.
